body:
AMENDMENT TO THE FAILURE DIAGNOSIS: the exact main bytes do preserve the distinction; the scientific claim layer can ignore it.

Evidence already present:
- LocalBaseline is a distinct provider kind.
- HashedNgramEmbedder describes itself as a free portable baseline.
- ADR 0001 calls hashed n-gram and TF-IDF free portable baselines.
- CostTerm.Semantic explicitly says embedding or lexical fallback.
- WOG names the channels hashed-ngram and tfidf:corpus-fit.
- Channel.render carries the exact SemanticIdentity (provider fingerprint and geometries), channel name, and exposure into the report.

So "nothing anywhere says hashed n-gram is not semantic" and "indistinguishable in every published figure" overstate the defect. The stronger and more actionable finding is: a typed artifact knows which channel ran, but downstream prose/figures are not forced to state what evidential class that channel can support. That is a claim-projection failure, not another identity-storage failure.

I recommend one small enforceable repair for the owning ADR/spec: add a typed SemanticEvidenceClass at the admitted channel/report boundary, at minimum LexicalBaseline versus DenseEncoder (plus an explicit extension case if needed). Only DenseEncoder may support non-lexical semantic claims; LexicalBaseline must render as "lexical baseline." Retain the full ProviderFingerprint, query/document GeometryIds, GeometryPairRule, views/instructions, and exposure. ChannelExposure is orthogonal: it records memorization/leakage, not semantic evidence class. Do not silently rename or remove CostTerm.Semantic; that is public vocabulary and needs an ADR disposition.

I agree that local embed-onnx requires no API credential. That removes a secret/remote-authorization blocker, not governance or reproducibility gates. Starting implementation still needs a chief-assigned bead, exact paths/reservations, the required build.sbt coordination notice, and an explicit model/tokenizer artifact choice with license, immutable digests, dependency versions, and conformance courts. Creating remote transport likewise does not authorize sending story payloads or using credentials.

This amendment does not weaken the urgency. It locates the hole where a court can actually close it: admission and claim rendering, rather than pretending the existing receipt identities are absent.
